# Flow: two-stage load (export parts, then build)

One-line summary: stage 1 keeps every Snowflake read as a Parquet part in `.cache/reads/<key>/`, so a load that stops resumes with only the missing parts; stage 2 builds the role graph, the rules and the copies from those parts without Snowflake (`cache.py:314-319`, README.md:162-165).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant R as run.py / page
    participant S as server.py
    participant P as cache.parted (parts)
    participant A as access.py (snapshot / live / each)
    participant SF as Snowflake
    participant C as cache.store
    R->>S: first page (load_shared) or run.py --export
    S->>S: tracked(KEY, "shared", stages)
    S->>A: with_query(fn, KEY): query = parted(query, KEY, OFFLINE)
    A->>P: each(query, sqls, what) -> query.keep(sqls, what, run)
    P->>P: take(name): part kept and ok? rows from parquet
    P->>SF: only the missing / timed-out parts (one login, at the first statement)
    SF-->>P: rows -> write_part + parts.json
    P-->>A: rows per statement (or the kept exception)
    A-->>S: snapshot / live dict
    S->>C: cache.get -> store: memory, .pkl, SQL copy thread
    S->>S: built(d): a.step build, a.step rule checks (or kept_rules)
    S-->>R: pages answer; "Ready in N s"
```

## Steps

1. `run.py --export [--fresh]` starts `python server.py --export` (`run.py:44-45`); `server.export(fresh)` clears the parts on `--fresh`, reads the shared data with progress lines on the terminal, builds nothing, prints the parts and the timed-out ones; all ok -> `cache.drop(KEY)` so the next start builds from the new parts, exit 0; else 1 — `server.py:2671-2691`, `server.py:2699-2700`.
2. A page load: `load_shared()` answers from memory / `.pkl` at once; Direct mode with no copy and no parts needs the click (409 `shared_not_loaded`); a load already running answers 409 `shared_loading` (the page never waits) — `server.py:177-196`. Else `tracked(KEY, "shared", stages)` — `server.py:190`.
3. `stages()`: stage 1 `cache.get(KEY, read_shared)`, stage 2 `built(d)`, then "Ready in N s" — `server.py:155-162`.
4. `read_shared(key)`: Direct mode starts from `cache.old(key, KEY)` (the earlier ACTIVITY / OBJECT_USE rows, kept as `old.pkl` with the parts, so a resumed load asks for the same days and its part names stay the same) — `server.py:139-147`, `cache.py:344-359`; objects mode passes `old=cache.last(KEY)` and `snapshot()` asks the last OK run through `query.fresh` on every load (never a part), so a newer run shows and an unchanged one reads no table again — `server.py:147`, `access.py:513-516`, `cache.py:550`.
5. `with_query(fn, key)`: the connection is made at the first statement that goes to Snowflake (one login across `each()`'s threads; a failed login fails every statement as `ConnectionError`), so a load answered from parts logs in to nothing; `query` is wrapped by `cache.parted(query, key, OFFLINE)` when disk is allowed — `server.py:82-105`.
6. `each()` hands a wave to `query.keep(sqls, what, run)` — `access.py:699-701`. `keep()`: heavy reads (a list of names) are a part each, kept the moment each answers; a wave of like statements is one part, and a wave whose statements timed out reads only those again (`cache.py:535-546`) — `cache.py:521-548`. Single statements go through `q(sql)` — `cache.py:510-519`.
7. Part names: label + sha1 of the statements (`part_name`, `cache.py:423-426`): another run or other days is another part. `take()` reads a kept part unless it failed (a timeout), rebuilding rows per statement from `__i` and the kept errors — `cache.py:437-453`. `put()` writes `<name>.parquet` with every column any statement of the wave answered (pyarrow, else DuckDB COPY; `.tmp` then rename) and the `parts.json` entry; a lost session is never kept; a part of mixed types stays in memory only — `cache.py:455-486`, `cache.py:387-406`.
8. A `USE` answered from its part is replayed before the next statement that goes to Snowflake — `cache.py:488-497`, `cache.py:515-516`.
9. `cache.get` -> `store(key, d)`: memory; `.pkl` (previous kept as `.prev.pkl`); the SQL copy in a `COPYING` thread; a read with no OK run stays in memory only — `cache.py:122-161`.
10. `built(d)`: under `LOCK`, `a.step("Building the role graph")` `a.build`, a count line, `a.step("Checking the rules")` unless `kept_rules()` put the results back, then saves them — `server.py:165-174`, `server.py:310-329`.
11. `run.py --build` sets `BUILD_ONLY=1` (`run.py:46-47`): `OFFLINE` (`server.py:26`) makes `parted(..., offline=True)` fail a missing part as "not exported yet (python run.py --export reads it)" and never connect — `cache.py:489-490`; refreshes answer `BUILD_ONLY_NOTE` — `server.py:2358-2359`.
12. Parts are read again only on Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again ([background-refresh.md](background-refresh.md)), a fresh My access load (`server.py:258`) or `--export --fresh`; "Data from" shows the oldest part's time (`fetched`, `server.py:199-202`, `cache.py:339-341`).

## Example (test_server.test_parts, fake connection)

- A first load keeps every read as a part; one part marked timed out -> the next load reads only that statement.
- `BUILD_ONLY=1` reads nothing from Snowflake; `--export --fresh` reads every part again; `run.command(["--export", "--fresh"])` -> `python server.py --export --fresh`, `--build` -> `BUILD_ONLY=1` — `test_server.py:950-989`.

## Unclear

- Parts have no age limit: data from an old export stays until a manual refresh or `--export --fresh` (`cache.py:314-319`); "Data from" shows its time (inferred: by design, README.md:165).

Rule: [business_rule:read_parts](../logic/rules.md). Data: [data/duckdb-copy.md](../data/duckdb-copy.md).
